attributes.residual: NEW DEAD AXIS: K&R old-style parameter declaration on the wrapper (void dcsHandleRequest(request, input, output) with separate u32/s32*/s32* declarators) measured EXACTLY NEUTRAL - real 144, insns 411/411, multiset 2t, identical cluster offsets. The project's named 'K&R passthrough' lever therefore does NOT re-rank nonvolatile web priority, closing the axis the v3 record asked for ('a genuinely new axis must re-rank the three formal webs' allocation priority'). Reverted by hand (probe banks NEUTRAL states, so git is the surgical revert). NEW DECOMPOSITION that v3 lacked, from tools/gdl/regnorm.py: 493 paired, 66 RENAMING, 2 STRUCTURAL, 2 unpaired -> STRUCTURAL-PRESENT. The 66 renaming rows are the 3-cycle formal permutation (target request=r28/input=r29/output=r30 in ascending formal order; ours input=r28/output=r29/request=r30), confirming v3's prologue-seed diagnosis. The 2 unpaired rows are the live-zero pair (UNPAIRED-T li r31,0 @0x260 vs UNPAIRED-O addi r30,r31,0 @0x25c). The 2 STRUCTURAL rows are NEW and unrecorded by v3: R_PPC_ADDR16_HA/LO at 0x40/0x44 where the target relocates the switch jump table against jumptable_80129618 while our object emits a local label @230 - the TU's data measures 100% so this reads as a symbol-name normalization artifact rather than a payload difference, but it should be confirmed before any flip attempt. CONSEQUENCE for the WebFrank route: the 66-row recolor is NOT eligible as a REGISTER_ONLY rule, because regnorm's own rule is that the REGISTER_ONLY label is honest only at 0 STRUCTURAL and 0 unpaired, and this function has 2 of each.
